title: The right-wing obsession with “The Indian Question”
gist: Yglesias argues conservatives' fixation on 'The Indian Question' reveals that opposition to immigration is really about ethnic change, since Indian Americans arrive through selective pathways and are an elite group (median household income over $150,000, 77 percent with college degrees). He notes his selective-immigration pitch won over conservative hosts who may not have realized it means many South Asian immigrants.

insights.claim: Because 900 million people say they would like to leave their country (Gallup), the US could substantially raise permanent residency slots while making the increase selective for above-average earners.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Argues the US has a large supply of high-earning immigrants, a growth and fiscal upside case.

insights.claim: Selective immigration in practice means many South Asian immigrants, which some conservatives who endorsed the idea may not have grasped.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Expect the right's support for merit-based immigration to fracture on who actually qualifies.

insights.claim: Indian Americans have median household income above $150,000 and 77 percent of those 25+ hold a college degree per Pew, and arrive via selective pathways, making them a clear economic and budget benefit.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Evidence that high-skill immigration is fiscally and economically positive.

insights.claim: Objection to Indian Americans reduces to objection to ethnic change as such, which Yglesias calls an ugly sentiment that will lead to bad consequences if indulged.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Signals nativist currents in the GOP that could constrain skilled-immigration reform.

insights.claim: Texas GOP railroad commissioner nominee Bo French tweeted about South Asian students at a University of Texas game, drawing backlash; Democrat Jon Rosenthal, a moderate oil and gas veteran, is his opponent.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Texas railroad commissioner race regulates oil and gas; a notable down-ballot election to watch.
